hazards.location_in_image: Foreground, along the curb line behind the parked SUV

hazards.name: Trip Hazards
hazards.description: Cracked pavement and overgrown weeds in the walkway create uneven surfaces.
hazards.location_in_image: Along the narrow concrete strip at the base of the stairs

hazards.name: Landscaping Obstruction
hazards.description: A tall, dense hedge on the left side of the image limits peripheral visibility for pedestrians and may hide them from approaching motorists.
hazards.location_in_image: Left foreground, adjacent to the sidewalk

hazards.name: Utility pole obstructions
hazards.description: Wooden utility poles are located directly in the center of the narrow sidewalk, restricting the clear path for pedestrians, especially those with mobility aids or strollers.
hazards.location_in_image: Right side of the image along the sidewalk

hazards.name: Visual Obstructions from Parking
hazards.description: Continuous parallel parking on both sides of the street obscures sight lines between pedestrians on the sidewalk and approaching drivers.
hazards.location_in_image: Both curbsides

hazards.name: Unmarked Roadway
hazards.description: The lack of lane markings on a wide residential street can lead to unpredictable vehicle positioning and higher speeds.
hazards.location_in_image: Center foreground roadway

hazards.name: Unmarked Intersection
hazards.description: The intersection ahead lacks marked crosswalks, forcing pedestrians to cross without designated space.
hazards.location_in_image: Center background

hazards.name: Degraded road surface
hazards.description: The asphalt shows significant cracking and wear, which can create hazards for cyclists or pedestrians crossing the street.
hazards.location_in_image: Roadway surface in the foreground

hazards.name: Lack of Protected Crossings
hazards.description: The long stretch of residential street lacks any marked crossing points or traffic calming measures to manage vehicle speeds.
hazards.location_in_image: Entire visible length of the roadway

hazards.name: Utility pole obstruction
hazards.description: A utility pole is placed in the middle of the narrow sidewalk, blocking the clear path for pedestrians, especially those using wheelchairs or strollers.
hazards.location_in_image: Center-left on the sidewalk

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install curb extensions (bulb-outs) at intersections to improve visibility and reduce the crossing distance for pedestrians.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Add marked crosswalks with high-visibility patterns at intersections to clearly define pedestrian right-of-way.

interventions.title: Street Trees
interventions.description: Incorporate street trees to provide a physical buffer between the sidewalk and the roadway while also narrowing the perceived width of the street.

interventions.title: Sidewalk Installation
interventions.description: Construct a continuous, ADA-compliant sidewalk to separate pedestrians from vehicle traffic.

interventions.title: Speed Humps
interventions.description: Install traffic calming measures to reduce vehicle speeds on this residential street.

interventions.title: Street Lighting
interventions.description: Add pedestrian-scale street lighting to improve visibility and safety at night.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions (Bulb-outs)
interventions.description: Extend the sidewalk into the parking lane to shorten crossing distances and improve visibility between drivers and pedestrians.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Refuge Island
interventions.description: Install a raised island in the center of the wide roadway to allow pedestrians to cross one direction of traffic at a time.

interventions.title: Leading Pedestrian Interval (LPI)
interventions.description: Program the traffic signals to give pedestrians a 3-7 second head start before vehicles get a green light.

interventions.title: Street Tree Planting
interventions.description: Replace the stump with a new street tree to restore the canopy and provide a vertical buffer between pedestrians and the street.

interventions.title: Buffer Strip
interventions.description: Introduce a small planting strip or furniture zone between the sidewalk and the curb to increase separation from traffic.

interventions.title: Parking Lot Screening
interventions.description: Install low-level fencing or landscaping between the sidewalk and the parking lot to better define the pedestrian realm.

interventions.title: Street Trees and Planting Strips
interventions.description: Add street trees to provide a physical and psychological buffer between the sidewalk and moving traffic, while also encouraging slower driving speeds.

interventions.title: Speed Humps or Cushions
interventions.description: Implement vertical traffic calming measures to reduce vehicle speeds in this mixed-use/residential area.

interventions.title: Traffic Calming Measures
interventions.description: Implement speed humps or cushions to ensure vehicle speeds remain low in this residential context.

interventions.title: Daylighting
interventions.description: Remove parking spaces closest to intersections or potential crossing points to improve sight lines.

interventions.title: Mid-block Crossing
interventions.description: If pedestrian demand is high, a marked mid-block crossing with appropriate signage could provide a safer crossing point.

interventions.title: Sidewalk Widening and Repair
interventions.description: Reconstruct the sidewalk to meet ADA standards for width and surface quality, potentially by reallocating a portion of the roadway.

interventions.title: Street Trees and Buffer Zone
interventions.description: Introduce street trees or a planting strip between the sidewalk and the curb to provide a physical and psychological buffer from moving traffic.

interventions.title: Traffic Calming
interventions.description: Implement speed humps or cushions to ensure vehicle speeds remain low in this residential context.

interventions.title: Street Trees and Buffer
interventions.description: Install a planting strip or street trees to provide a physical and psychological buffer between pedestrians and traffic.

interventions.title: Sidewalk Widening
interventions.description: Increase the width of the sidewalk to accommodate pedestrians and necessary street furniture or trash storage without blocking the path.

interventions.title: Lane Markings
interventions.description: Add painted lane lines to narrow the perceived travel lanes, which naturally encourages slower driving speeds.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Lighting
interventions.description: Installing pedestrian-scale street lighting to improve visibility and safety during nighttime hours.

interventions.title: Street Trees and Buffers
interventions.description: Introduce a planting strip or street trees between the sidewalk and the curb to provide a safety buffer.

interventions.title: Utility Relocation
interventions.description: Move utility poles out of the sidewalk clear zone to ensure an unobstructed path.
